attention.pdf: We propose the Transformer, a network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms.
Multi-head attention lets the model attend to information from different representation subspaces.
mamba.pdf: Selective state space models give linear-time sequence modeling.
Unlike attention, the cost grows linearly with the length of the input sequence.
bert.pdf: BERT pre-trains deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text.
Masked language modeling hides some tokens and predicts them from context.
diffusion.pdf: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models generate images by reversing a noising process.
Sample quality on CIFAR10 reaches an FID score of 3.17.
resnet.pdf: Deep residual learning eases the training of very deep convolutional networks.
Shortcut connections add the input of a block to its output.
rag.pdf: Retrieval-augmented generation combines a retriever with a sequence-to-sequence generator.
The generator conditions on passages fetched from a Wikipedia index.
adam.pdf: Adam is an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objectives.
It keeps running averages of the gradient and its square to adapt learning rates.
dropout.pdf: Dropout randomly drops units during training to prevent co-adaptation.
It is a simple way to reduce overfitting in large neural networks.
word2vec.pdf: We learn continuous vector representations of words from very large corpora.
Skip-gram predicts the surrounding words given the current word.
gan.pdf: Generative adversarial networks train a generator against a discriminator.
The discriminator learns to tell real samples from generated ones.
sicp.pdf: Programs must be written for people to read, and only incidentally for machines to execute.
Procedures are abstractions that let us name and reuse computations.
ddia.pdf: Replication keeps a copy of the same data on several machines connected by a network.
Partitioning splits a large dataset into smaller subsets across nodes.
